title: Qcqs pro-etale subsite and finite limits
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be its full subcategory on quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with finite pro-etale covering families [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Then $\mathcal C$ is a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], has fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] computed as scheme fibre products, and its inclusion into $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ preserves fibre products and sends coverings to coverings. For every $T\in\mathcal C$, the slice $\mathcal C/T$ has finite limits computed as scheme limits over $T$. If $X$ itself is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $\mathcal C$ has finite limits computed as scheme limits over $X$. Adjoining finitely many arrows of $\mathcal C$ with the same target to a finite covering family preserves the covering property.

proof.text: For $U\to T\leftarrow V$ in $\mathcal C$, both arrows are weakly etale by the between-objects lemma. The scheme fibre product $P=U\times_T V$ exists. Its projection to $V$ is weakly etale by base change, hence $P\to X$ is weakly etale by composition. By qcqs permanence (1), $U\to T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; (3) gives these properties for $P\to V$, and (2) gives that $P$ is qcqs. The scheme universal property restricts to the full subcategory, with the induced arrows over $X$, proving existence and preservation of fibre products.

The full pro-etale category is a site as specified in its definition. An isomorphism with qcqs target has qcqs source, so its singleton covering belongs to $\mathcal C$. Composing a finite covering with one finite covering for each of its finitely many sources gives a finite covering in the full site, with all sources still in $\mathcal C$. Pullback of a finite covering along an arrow of $\mathcal C$ is a covering in the full site with the same finite index set; step 1 puts its sources in $\mathcal C$. These are exactly the three site axioms. Coverings are sent to coverings by their definition.

Fix $T\in\mathcal C$. The slice has terminal object $T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}T$ and binary products from step 1. For parallel arrows $a,b:U\rightrightarrows V$ over $T$, construct $E=U\times_{V\times_T V}V$, using $(a,b)$ and $\Delta_{V/T}$. Both $V\times_T V$ and $E$ are in $\mathcal C$ by step 1. A morphism to $E$ is uniquely a morphism $c$ to $U$ with $ac=bc$, since its $V$-component must equal $ac$; this proves the equalizer universal property. For a finite diagram, form the product of its objects and the product of one target object for each diagram arrow; the two maps to the latter product have components given by the source projection followed by the arrow, and the target projection. Their equalizer is the limit. Empty products are $T$. Each construction has the same universal property in schemes over $T$. If $X$ is qcqs, it is terminal in $\mathcal C$, and this construction with $T=X$ gives finite limits there.

Every additional arrow in $\mathcal C$ is weakly etale by the between-objects lemma. For each affine open of the target, keep the finite list of affine source opens witnessing the original fpqc covering; their images still cover that affine open after more arrows are adjoined. Thus the enlarged family is pro-etale covering by its definition, and the union of its two finite index sets is finite.
